_comment: Server-side register of the numbered normative statements of MQTT 5.0 and MQTT 3.1.1 for mqttiumd. Maintained by hand; see README.md in this directory for the meaning of every field and status. `python3 mqttiumd/conformance/check.py` checks it and rewrites SUMMARY.md.

5.0.note: Every received string passes `Cursor::string`; the test refuses an overlong sequence in a ClientID. Surrogates are refused by the same `from_utf8` call but are not asserted.
A ClientID containing U+0000 is refused as malformed, and a filter containing it is not a valid filter.
A ClientID starting with EF BB BF is kept byte for byte.

A non-minimal Remaining Length is malformed and closes the connection; sent lengths are checked at the 128 and 16,384 boundaries. The same rule for a Property Length (`Cursor::variable`) is not asserted.
Both strings of a User Property are read with `Cursor::string`; no test sends an invalid one.
A PUBREL with flag bits 0000 is malformed, and the first byte of the sent CONNACK, PUBREC and PINGRESP is asserted. The other reserved-flag cases of `flags` are not asserted one by one.
A received QoS 0 PUBLISH decodes without an identifier and the sent one is compared byte for byte.
Binds the client only.
Core level: two outgoing deliveries get identifiers 1 and 2, and an identifier stays unavailable until the finish of its exchange is known.
PUBACK and PUBREC are read from the socket with the identifier of their PUBLISH; PUBCOMP and the broker's own PUBREL are asserted at core level.
The acknowledgement is built from the identifier of the request, but no test compares the identifier of a SUBACK or UNSUBACK with the one sent.
A sent PUBLISH without properties carries a zero Property Length, and a SUBSCRIBE without one is malformed.
Binds the client only. A first packet other than CONNECT closes the connection (`packet_before_connack`).
A second CONNECT closes the connection (event `second_connect`) without a DISCONNECT. No test of the product runtime sends one.
Any other protocol name is malformed: the connection is closed without a CONNACK. Not asserted.

Level 4 is served as MQTT 3.1.1. Any other level gets a 3.1.1-format CONNACK with return code 1 (asserted on the encoder) and the connection is closed; the closing path is asserted with another refusal cause.
A set reserved flag is `ReservedConnectFlag`, malformed, closed without a CONNACK. Not asserted.
Clean Start replaces a stored session by a new one with Session Present 0. The socket-level test exists in the `test-hooks` build only; the store and core tests run in both.
A reconnection with Clean Start 0 gets Session Present 1, keeps its subscription and receives the messages queued while it was away.
An unknown ClientID with Clean Start 0 gets a new session and Session Present 0.
The Will is durable in the store before the CONNECT result is relayed. Only a QoS 1, zero-delay, property-free Will is accepted.

The Will is admitted once after DISCONNECT 0x04, after a take-over and after a restart, and not after DISCONNECT 0x00. A non-zero Will Delay Interval is refused, so that branch does not exist; no test reads the Will PUBLISH on a subscriber's socket.
A CONNECT with the Will Flag and no Will fields is malformed.
The stored Will is gone after DISCONNECT 0x00 and after its publication.
Will Flag 0 with a non-zero Will QoS is `InvalidWillFlags`.
Only Will QoS 1 is accepted: a CONNECT with Will QoS 0 or 2 is answered with CONNACK 0x83 and closed. Will QoS 3 is a Protocol Error closed without a CONNACK.
Will Flag 0 with Will Retain 1 is `InvalidWillFlags`.
The retain bit of the stored Will selects the retained admission; no test asserts that a Will with Will Retain 0 leaves no retained message.
Store level: a Will with Will Retain 1 becomes the retained message of its topic and outlives its source.
Fields are read according to the flags and any byte left over is `TrailingFields`, malformed. Not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK 0x83 and closed.
Fields are read according to the flags and any byte left over is `TrailingFields`, malformed. Not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK 0x83 and closed.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only. The broker sends no Server Keep Alive.
A connection without a decoded packet for more than 1.5 times its Keep Alive is closed (`keep_alive`), checked on the reactor's idle tick. No maintained test waits for it.
A session with a finite or infinite interval survives its connection and a graceful stop; one with interval 0 does not.
A refusal larger than the client's limit is not written, and a PUBLISH above it is never emitted. See MQTT-3.1.2-25 for what happens instead.

Non-conformant for QoS 1 and 2: `plan_delivery_emit` closes the connection (CapacityExceeded, no DISCONNECT) and keeps the delivery, so each reconnection of that session is closed at the same message; `product_pubsub_delivery_over_peer_maximum_packet_size_is_discarded_and_the_next_one_sent` states the required behaviour and fails on this code. A QoS 0 copy is discarded as required (`qos0_fits`).
The broker never sends a Topic Alias: `encode_publication` writes no property or the Message Expiry Interval only, and the encoder tests compare whole packets.
The broker never sends a Topic Alias: `encode_publication` writes no property or the Message Expiry Interval only, and the encoder tests compare whole packets.
The CONNACK is a fixed layout without Response Information. A CONNECT with Request Response Information 1 is refused with CONNACK 0x83.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. Request Problem Information is parsed and needs no further handling.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only. The broker reads the fields in that order.
The session found at reconnection, with its subscription and queued messages, is the one of the ClientID.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only. The broker reads it with `Cursor::string`.
ClientIDs up to 1,024 bytes are accepted. The tests use a few identifiers, not the whole alphabet and every length; on the mTLS listener the ClientID must also be granted to the certificate.
A zero-length ClientID is not allowed: CONNACK 0x85, then the connection is closed. Nothing is assigned.
A zero-length ClientID is not allowed: CONNACK 0x85, then the connection is closed. No Assigned Client Identifier is ever sent.
An empty ClientID gets CONNACK 0x85 and one above 1,024 bytes CONNACK 0x95, then the connection is closed. The MQTT 5 bytes for these two causes are not asserted.
A non-zero Will Delay Interval is refused with CONNACK 0x83 (`will_profile_refusals_do_not_accept_ignored_properties`), so no delayed Will exists to withhold.
A Will carrying a User Property, or any property other than a zero Will Delay Interval, is refused with CONNACK 0x83.
The Will Topic is read with `Cursor::string` and checked as a Topic Name; ill-formed UTF-8 in it is not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK 0x83 and closed.

Codec level: malformed and contradictory CONNECT packets are refused. On the socket, the close of a refused CONNECT that gets no CONNACK is asserted with a well-formed one; no runtime test sends a malformed CONNECT.

On the mTLS listener a ClientID or Will topic not granted to the certificate gets CONNACK 0x87 and the connection is closed. The policy is unit-tested, the refusal path is not; the plaintext listener authenticates nobody.
The previous connection of the ClientID reads DISCONNECT 0x8E and is closed before the new session opens.
Both values of Clean Start are exercised against a stored session.
An accepted CONNECT is answered with CONNACK reason 0x00, on the runtime and on the real executable.
A refused connection is marked closing and its input is no longer read. No test sends data after a refused CONNECT.
With CONNECT and a second packet in one write, nothing is sent before the CONNACK.
A second CONNECT closes the connection before any second CONNACK could be produced. Not asserted.
The acknowledge flags byte is 0 or 1 in every CONNACK the encoder produces.
Clean Start over a stored session answers Session Present 0. The socket-level test exists in the `test-hooks` build only.
Session Present is 1 for a stored session and 0 for an unknown ClientID, read from the socket.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only.

After a refusing CONNACK the connection is gone.

The condition does not arise: QoS 0, 1 and 2 publications are accepted, and the CONNACK carries no Maximum QoS.
The condition does not arise: QoS 0, 1 and 2 publications are accepted. SUBSCRIBE is granted the QoS it requests.

Store and core level: a retained publication is stored without subscribers and replaces the previous one.
Store level: an empty retained publication removes the stored value and is still published live.
Store level: after the empty publication the retained table is empty.

Store level: a subscription with Retain Handling 0 is owed every matching retained message.
Store level: with Retain Handling 1 a new subscription is replayed and a repeated one is not.
Store level, asserted through one filter subscribed three times (Retain Handling 2, 1, 0): only the last adds replays.
Component level: routing computes the per-destination flag and the store keeps it per delivery. No test reads the RETAIN bit of a forwarded PUBLISH on a socket.
Component level: routing computes the per-destination flag and the store keeps it per delivery. No test reads the RETAIN bit of a forwarded PUBLISH on a socket.

Will Flag 0 with a non-zero Will QoS is `InvalidWillFlags`, asserted on an MQTT 5 CONNECT.

The retain bit of the stored Will selects the retained admission; no test asserts that a Will with Will Retain 0 leaves no retained message.

ClientIDs up to 1,024 bytes are accepted. The tests use a few identifiers, not the whole alphabet and every length; on the mTLS listener the ClientID must also be granted to the certificate.
A zero-length ClientID is not allowed, whatever CleanSession says: return code 0x02, then the connection is closed. Nothing is assigned.
Binds the client only.
A zero-length ClientID with CleanSession 0 is answered with return code 0x02, asserted on the encoder; the socket path that writes it and closes is asserted with an MQTT 5 refusal only.
A refused ClientID (empty, or above 1,024 bytes) maps to return code 0x02; the empty case is asserted on the encoder.
The Will Topic is read with `Cursor::string` and checked as a Topic Name; ill-formed UTF-8 in it is not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK return code 0x04 and closed.
A malformed CONNECT carries no validated response limit, so nothing is written and the connection is closed. No test asserts the absence of a CONNACK for a malformed 3.1.1 CONNECT.
A 3.1.1 predecessor is closed without a packet. The take-over tests drive MQTT 5 connections, whose branch writes DISCONNECT 0x8E first; the 3.1.1 branch is not exercised.
Both values of CleanSession are decoded and both session paths are exercised. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
The 3.1.1 CONNACK of an accepted CONNECT is 20 02 with return code 0.
A refused connection is marked closing and its input is no longer read. No test sends data after a refused CONNECT.

With CONNECT and a second packet in one write, nothing is sent before the CONNACK. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
A clean open reports no stored session (store and runtime), and the 3.1.1 CONNACK encodes that as 0.
Session Present 1 is read from the socket for a stored session. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
Session Present 0 is read from the socket for an unknown ClientID. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
Every refusing 3.1.1 CONNACK is 20 02 00 followed by the return code.
After a refusing CONNACK the connection is gone. The test refuses an MQTT 5 CONNECT; the same lines write and close for 3.1.1.
A refusal without a specific return code is sent as 0x03 (Server unavailable); only a malformed CONNECT is closed without a CONNACK. Neither choice is asserted.
Core level: a delivery replayed after reconnection carries DUP 1. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
The 3.1.1 QoS 0 PUBLISH is written with first byte 0x30.
The outgoing DUP is `may_have_started` of the delivery and the incoming DUP is not stored; no test varies the incoming flag and observes the outgoing one.
QoS 3 is `InvalidQos` in the header parser and the reader closes the connection (`malformed_header`). Not asserted.
Store level: the retained message is kept with its QoS, without subscribers and after its producer is gone.
Store level: a new subscription is owed every matching retained message.
A QoS 0 retained publication is stored. The replacement of a previous value is asserted with QoS 1 and 2 publications, not with QoS 0.
Store level: a replayed delivery carries the retain mark. The 3.1.1 writer keeps it only for a replay (`try_submit`), which no test reads on a socket.
For a 3.1.1 connection the writer clears RETAIN unless the delivery is a retained replay; this version-specific branch is not exercised.
Store level: an empty retained publication removes the stored value and is still published live.
Store level: after the empty publication the retained table is empty.
Only a PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 produces the retained recipe; no test asserts that a non-retained publication leaves an existing retained message in place.
The Topic Name is the first field of the decoded and of the written 3.1.1 PUBLISH.
A PUBLISH to `a/+` is refused; the check is shared and asserted on the MQTT 5 layout.
A destination is selected only when its filter matches the published Topic Name, which is forwarded unchanged; the forwarded name is not compared on a socket.
QoS 1 is answered with PUBACK and QoS 2 with PUBREC. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
Core level: overlapping subscriptions of one session give one delivery at their maximum QoS.
On the mTLS listener a PUBLISH to a topic not granted closes the 3.1.1 connection without a packet. The policy is unit-tested, the refusal path is not.
A 3.1.1 PUBREL with flag bits 1010 is refused.
Flag bits other than 0010 are `InvalidFixedFlags` and the reader closes the connection. Not asserted for SUBSCRIBE.
Each filter is read with `Cursor::string`; ill-formed UTF-8 in a filter is not asserted.
The condition does not arise: filters with wildcards are supported.
A SUBSCRIBE without a filter is `EmptySubscriptionList` and the connection is closed. Not asserted.

Ordinary filters are answered with a SUBACK (asserted on MQTT 5 connections). Non-conformant corner: `codec::filter` applies the MQTT 5 `$share/` grammar to 3.1.1 too, so a SUBSCRIBE to `$share/x`, a valid 3.1.1 filter, is a Protocol Error and the connection is closed without a SUBACK.
The SUBACK is built from the identifier of the SUBSCRIBE; no test compares the two.

One route remains after a repeated filter, its retained messages are replayed and a delivery already owed survives. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
Core level: two filters in one SUBSCRIBE are applied in order and answered by one SUBACK.
One return code per filter: the granted QoS, or 0x80 for any failure.
Core and store level: a delivery has the minimum of the published and granted QoS; the granted QoS is the requested one.
Core level: the results [2, 0] follow the order of the two filters.
The 3.1.1 encoder maps every result above 2 to 0x80.
Flag bits other than 0010 are `InvalidFixedFlags` and the reader closes the connection. Not asserted for UNSUBSCRIBE.
Each filter is read with `Cursor::string`; ill-formed UTF-8 in a filter is not asserted.
An UNSUBSCRIBE without a filter is `EmptySubscriptionList` and the connection is closed. Not asserted.
Core level: UNSUBSCRIBE `a/+` leaves the subscription `a/#`; the exact filter removes it.
Core level: the route is removed when the UNSUBACK is produced. No test publishes afterwards and observes that nothing is delivered.
Core level: a delivery admitted before the UNSUBSCRIBE is still claimed and sent.

Ordinary filters are answered with an UNSUBACK (core test, 3.1.1 encoder test); its identifier is not compared with the request. Non-conformant corner: for a `$share/` filter the core answers 0x8F, which `encode_for` cannot express in 3.1.1, and the connection is closed without an UNSUBACK (`failure_without_wire_ack`).
An UNSUBSCRIBE that removes nothing gives the result 0x11, which the 3.1.1 encoder writes as a plain UNSUBACK.
The filters are applied in order into one UNSUBACK; no test sends an UNSUBSCRIBE with several filters.
A PINGREQ written to the socket is answered with PINGRESP. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
Non-zero flag bits are `InvalidFixedFlags` and the reader closes the connection; no test sends a DISCONNECT with reserved bits. A 3.1.1 DISCONNECT with a body is refused (asserted).
Binds the client only.
In MQTT 3.1.1 only the Client sends DISCONNECT, so this binds the client. The broker closes the connection when it receives one.
A 3.1.1 DISCONNECT decodes to 'do not publish the Will', and that disposition cancels the stored Will.

Subscriptions and queued messages are kept while the session exists, across a disconnection and a graceful stop. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
A session is never ended while its connection is attached. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
The 3.1.1 QoS 0 PUBLISH is written with first byte 0x30: QoS 0, DUP 0.

Core level: a new delivery draws an unused identifier, is first sent with DUP 0 and stays owed until its PUBACK. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
PUBACK carries the identifier of the PUBLISH after the durable admission, and a reused identifier is a new publication.

Core level: PUBREL follows the committed PUBREC with the same identifier, the exchange stays open until PUBCOMP and PUBLISH is not sent again after PUBREL. The first emission's DUP 0 is asserted for QoS 1 only.
Core level: PUBREC after the admission, PUBREC again without a second admission for a repeated PUBLISH, PUBCOMP after the release, and a new exchange for a reused identifier.

Core level: unacknowledged PUBLISH and PUBREL are replayed with their identifiers after a reconnection. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.

A QoS 1 publication is stored for the matching offline session and delivered at reconnection. The deciding code is shared by both protocol versions; the test drives it with an MQTT 5 connection or below the wire.
